title: ARTEX C406-N EMERGENCY LOCATOR TRANSMITTER - INSPECTION/CHECK
question: What are the key safety precautions and operational guidelines to follow when testing and maintaining the Artex 0406-N ELT system?
answer: CAUTION: Operate the Emergency Locator Transmitter system only during the first five minutes of each hour. The ELT will transmit a 406.028 MHz signal after the ELT is active for approximately 50 seconds. This signal is identified as a distress signalPrepare for the Artex 0406-N ELT Functional Test. (1) You must replace the ELT battery with a new ELT battery if one or more of the conditions that follow occur: Use of the ELT battery in an emergency Operation for an unknown amount of time Use for more than one hour of cumulative time On or before the replacement date shown on the battery label. (2)  Examine the ELT battery to make sure that it is not due for replacement. (3) If the battery must be replaced, follow the manufacturer's instructions to replace it. (4) Supply +28 v, +0.25 or -0.25 v, external electrical power to the airplane. (5) Initialize the global positioning system  on the multi-function display .Do the ELT Transmitter Test. (1) Adjust the volume to make sure that the transmissions from the radio are heard in the cockpit. (2) Adjust the COM 1 frequency to 121.50 MHz. Make sure that the audio is heard through the cockpit speakers. (3)  Put the cockpit ELT switch in the ON position for approximately one second. (4) Make sure that the ELT audio signal and the cockpit ELT switch light adjacent to the ELT remote switch come on. (5)  Immediately put the cockpit ELT switch in the ARM position. (6) Make sure that the LED stays on for approximately one second before it goes off. (7) If the ELT system has sensed a fault in the system, the LED will flash a fault code at this time. Refer to the Installation and Operation Manual for the Artex ELT system for information on the possible codes.

question: What are the detailed procedures for verifying the SARSAT interface and G-switch operation during the aircraft's ELT system testing?
answer: Do the NAV Interface Test. (1)  Hold the SARSAT tester no more than fifteen feet from the antenna. NOTE:  The SARSAT tester is used as an example to gather test information. However, other equivalent test equipment such as the Aeroflex IFR 4000 Communications Test Set is acceptable. (2)  Turn on the SARSAT tester. (3) Engage the receive function of the SARSAT tester. (4)  Make sure that the display on the tester shows that it is searching for a signal. (5)  Put the ELT remote switch in the ON position. (6) Within 15 seconds, put the ELT remote switch in the ARM position. (7) Monitor the SARSAT tester to see if it received a signal from the ELT system. (a) If no signal was received, do the test again after the 15-second off cycle. (8) Make sure that the tail number on the SARSAT tester is correct. (9) Make sure that the Mode S code shown on the SARSAT tester is the same as the number that is on the back of the transmitter. Disconnect external electrical power from the aircraft.Do the G-Switch Operational Test. CAUTION: Operate the Emergency Locator Transmitter system only during the first five minutes of each hour. If you must complete the functional test at a time other than the first five minutes of the hour, you must do the test with a direct connection to the ELT and a 30 dB attenuator. Refer to the FAA Advisory Circular AC-91 -44A. Do not operate the emergency locator transmitter for more than five seconds at a time. Do not operate the ELT again for 15 seconds. The ELT will transmit a 406.028 MHz signal after the ELT is active for approximately 50 seconds. This signal is identified as a distress signal. (1) Remove the ELT from the airplane. Refer to ELT Removal/Installation   Install a jumper wire between pins 12 and 13 on the electrical connector of the ELT. NOTE:  The ELT will not activate with the G-switch unless electrical pins 12 and 13 have a jumper wire installed between them . (6) Make sure that the G-switch operates and that the aural warning sweep tone is heard on the receiver set to 121 .5 MHz. (7) Set the ELT switch to the ON position and then back to the OFF position to reset the G-switch. (8) Remove the jumper wire from electrical pins 12 and 13 on the electrical connector of the ELT. title: ARTEX C406-N EMERGENCY LOCATOR TRANSMITTER - INSPECTION/CHECK
question: What are the necessary steps to verify the proper operation of the SARSAT interface and G-switch during the ELT system testing procedures?
answer: Do the NAV Interface Test. (1)  Hold the SARSAT tester no more than fifteen feet from the antenna. NOTE:  The SARSAT tester is used as an example to gather test information. However, other equivalent test equipment such as the Aeroflex IFR 4000 Communications Test Set is acceptable. (2)  Turn on the SARSAT tester. (3) Engage the receive function of the SARSAT tester. (4)  Make sure that the display on the tester shows that it is searching for a signal. (5)  Put the ELT remote switch in the ON position. (6) Within 15 seconds, put the ELT remote switch in the ARM position. (7) Monitor the SARSAT tester to see if it received a signal from the ELT system. (a) If no signal was received, do the test again after the 15-second off cycle. (8) Make sure that the tail number on the SARSAT tester is correct. (9) Make sure that the Mode S code shown on the SARSAT tester is the same as the number that is on the back of the transmitter.  Make sure that the latitude and longitude information is the same as that shown on the MFD display.  Turn the SARSAT tester off.  Disconnect external electrical power from the aircraft.Do the G-Switch Operational Test. CAUTION: Operate the Emergency Locator Transmitter system only during the first five minutes of each hour. If you must complete the functional test at a time other than the first five minutes of the hour, you must do the test with a direct connection to the ELT and a 30 dB attenuator. Refer to the FAA Advisory Circular AC-91 -44A. Do not operate the emergency locator transmitter for more than five seconds at a time. Do not operate the ELT again for 15 seconds. The ELT will transmit a 406.028 MHz signal after the ELT is active for approximately 50 seconds. This signal is identified as a distress signal. (1) Remove the ELT from the airplane. Refer to ELT Removal/Installation   Install a jumper wire between pins 12 and 13 on the electrical connector of the ELT. NOTE:  The ELT will not activate with the G-switch unless electrical pins 12 and 13 have a jumper wire installed between them . Because of the potential physical damage that can occur if the jumper wire is not installed correctly, it is recommended that an experienced technician do this procedure. (3) Put the ELT switch in the OFF position. (4) Use a receiver, and set it to 121 .5 MHz to listen for the aural warning sweep tone. (5) Hold the ELT transmitter tightly in one hand and make a throwing movement followed by an opposite movement of the ELT transmitter. (6) Make sure that the G-switch operates and that the aural warning sweep tone is heard on the receiver set to 121 .5 MHz. (7) Set the ELT switch to the ON position and then back to the OFF position to reset the G-switch. (8) Remove the jumper wire from electrical pins 12 and 13 on the electrical connector of the ELT. (9) Install the emergency locator transmitter in the airplane. Refer to ELT Removal/Installation (On airplanes with the Artex C406-N.

title: ARTEX C406-N EMERGENCY LOCATOR TRANSMITTER - INSPECTION/CHECK
question: What are the key safety and procedural considerations when performing the ELT functional test outside the first five minutes of each hour, including the use of a direct connection and attenuator?
answer: CAUTION: Operate the Emergency Locator Transmitter system only during the first five minutes of each hour. If you must complete the functional test at a time other than the first five minutes of the hour, you must do the test with a direct connection to the ELT and a 30 dB attenuator. Refer to the FAA Advisory Circular AC-91-44A. CAUTION: Do not operate the emergency locator transmitter for more than five seconds at a time.  Do not operate the ELT again for 15 seconds. (1) You must replace the ELT battery with a new ELT battery if one or more of the conditions that follow occur: Use of the ELT battery in an emergency Operation for an unknown amount of time Use for more than one hour of cumulative time On or before the replacement date shown on the battery label. (2)  Examine the ELT battery to make sure that it is not due for replacement. (3) If the battery must be replaced, follow the manufacturer's instructions to replace it. (4) Supply +28 v, +0.25 or -0.25 v, external electrical power to the airplane. (5) Initialize the global positioning system  on the multi-function display .Do the ELT Transmitter Test. (1) Adjust the volume to make sure that the transmissions from the radio are heard in the cockpit. (2) Adjust the COM 1 frequency to 121.50 MHz. Make sure that the audio is heard through the cockpit speakers. (3)  Put the cockpit ELT switch in the ON position for approximately one second. (4) Make sure that the ELT audio signal and the cockpit ELT switch light adjacent to the ELT remote switch come on. (5)  Immediately put the cockpit ELT switch in the ARM position. (6) Make sure that the LED stays on for approximately one second before it goes off. (7) If the ELT system has sensed a fault in the system, the LED will flash a fault code at this time. title: ARTEX C406-N EMERGENCY LOCATOR TRANSMITTER - INSPECTION/CHECK
question: What are the detailed procedures for verifying the SARSAT interface and G-switch operation during the ELT system testing process?
answer: Do the NAV Interface Test. (1)  Hold the SARSAT tester no more than fifteen feet from the antenna. NOTE:  The SARSAT tester is used as an example to gather test information. However, other equivalent test equipment such as the Aeroflex IFR 4000 Communications Test Set is acceptable. (2)  Turn on the SARSAT tester. (3) Engage the receive function of the SARSAT tester. (4)  Make sure that the display on the tester shows that it is searching for a signal. (5)  Put the ELT remote switch in the ON position. (6) Within 15 seconds, put the ELT remote switch in the ARM position. (7) Monitor the SARSAT tester to see if it received a signal from the ELT system. (a) If no signal was received, do the test again after the 15-second off cycle. (8) Make sure that the tail number on the SARSAT tester is correct. (9) Make sure that the Mode S code shown on the SARSAT tester is the same as the number that is on the back of the transmitter.  Make sure that the latitude and longitude information is the same as that shown on the MFD display.  Turn the SARSAT tester off.
